title: Snare synthesis parameters
description: Synthesis parameters for one deterministic snare sample (v0.1, proposal, #272). Mono. Only schema_version and seed are required; an omitted field takes the default named in its description. Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped. Voice: a pitched body of two sine partials (lower at body_hz, upper at body_hz * mode_ratio, both with the same exponential pitch drop) plus shaped noise (low-pass, a wide band and a narrow high-passed band with their own decays), mixed by body_level. Time t is measured from the first sample of the sound (sample n_off with offset_ms). All numeric ranges and defaults are PROPOSALS from docs/research/2026-11-02_snare-targets.md section 5 and docs/research/2026-11-02_snare-rim-and-sub-bass-design.md section 2.2 (S1 corrected); they are placeholders until the audio-engineer measures them and the user listens. The audio-engineer may adjust them in the engine PR (a contract-change then). Not part of v0.1: `snappy` (vocabulary keyword weight only), rim shot (a separate future `rim-params`, not a `model` of snare), `gate_ms`, `body_shape` (the body is sine), a note-name resolver for `body_hz`.
$comment: Contract rules that JSON Schema cannot express or that are not field ranges. (1) Cross-field rule: noise_lp_hz must be greater than 1.2 * noise_hp_hz. The schema cannot compare two fields, so the engine rejects a violation with an error text (never clamps) and tests check it. An omitted partner can never break the rule: with the default noise_lp_hz (9000) every noise_hp_hz in range satisfies it (1.2 * 6000 = 7200), and with the default noise_hp_hz (1800) every noise_lp_hz in range does (3000 > 2160). noise_lp_hz is below Nyquist for both sample rates. (2) Body: sine only in v0.1 (no body_shape). The upper partial is body_hz * mode_ratio and follows the pitch drop: both partials are multiplied by the same exponential curve from pitch_drop (start/end frequency ratio) at t = 0 down to 1 over pitch_drop_ms, so their ratio is mode_ratio at every instant. The highest instantaneous partial frequency body_hz * mode_ratio * pitch_drop is at most 400 * 2.4 * 2.0 = 1920 Hz, below 0.45 * sample_rate for both sample rates, so no cross-field rule is needed. (3) Decay: body_decay_ms and noise_decay_ms are the time from the end of the attack until that envelope has fallen 60 dB (time to -60 dB after the attack), exponential, same definition as kick amp_decay_ms and hat decay_ms. The upper partial decays in body_decay_ms * body2_decay_ratio; the narrow noise band has its own faster decay set by the engine PR from noise_decay_ms (its ratio is not a field in v0.1). (4) `body_level` is the share of PASSBAND POWER AFTER THE NOISE FILTERS: the body and the noise are each RMS-normalised after noise_hp_hz / noise_lp_hz (and the tone-peak stage if used) and mixed as sqrt(body_level) * body + sqrt(1 - body_level) * noise, so the body carries the share body_level of the mixed power; the same reading as hat `metal` (hat-params, $comment point 3). The body is not filtered by the noise filters. (5) Determinism: the body has no randomness; the seed changes only the noise, each noise layer (wide band, narrow band) takes its own sub-stream. At body_level 1 the output is seed-independent. (6) Reject out-of-range values, never clamp. Defaults are placeholders until measured. (7) The file ends with a 5 ms linear fade-out like the kick, the first sample is 0, DC is removed as in clap. length_ms: a given length_ms shorter than the sound cuts it with the fade; if omitted the engine uses 400 ms and records it in the sidecar. Shared field names keep the meaning of clap-params and kick-params (seed, variants, bpm, sample_rate, bit_depth, drive, polarity, offset_ms, peak_ceiling_dbfs, preset); length_ms has its own range here. Engine identity for sidecars: engine.name 'abeltongod-audio-engine-snare' with the snare engine's own version (sample-metadata.schema.json, D-025).

seed.description: Seeds the noise (one sub-stream per noise layer). The body is deterministic. Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV.

length_ms.description: File length. If shorter than the sound needs, it is cut off and gets a 5 ms fade-out.

body_hz.description: Frequency of the lower partial at the end of the pitch drop, Hz.

mode_ratio.description: Upper partial frequency = body_hz * mode_ratio, at every instant (it follows the pitch drop).

pitch_drop.description: Start frequency / end frequency of both partials. 1 = no drop.

pitch_drop_ms.description: Time constant span of the exponential pitch drop, ms. No effect at pitch_drop 1.

body_decay_ms.description: Time to fall 60 dB after the attack for the lower partial, exponential.

body2_decay_ratio.description: Decay of the upper partial relative to body_decay_ms.

body_level.description: Share of passband power after the noise filters that comes from the body; the rest is noise. 0 = noise only, 1 = body only (seed-independent).

noise_decay_ms.description: Time to fall 60 dB after the attack for the wide noise band, exponential.

noise_band_mix.description: Share of the narrow high-passed noise band, which has its own faster decay. 0 = wide band only.

noise_hp_hz.description: Corner of the noise high-pass, Hz. noise_lp_hz must be greater than 1.2 * noise_hp_hz.

noise_lp_hz.description: Corner of the noise low-pass, Hz. Must be greater than 1.2 * noise_hp_hz (cross-field rule, checked by the engine).

noise_attack_ms.description: Linear attack time of the noise, ms.

tone_peak_hz.description: Centre of a static peaking filter, Hz. No effect at tone_peak_db 0.

tone_peak_db.description: Gain of the peaking filter, dB. 0 = off.

drive.description: Anti-aliased saturation, same stage as kick drive. 0 = off.

polarity.description: Sign of the whole output, applied after the peak ceiling.

offset_ms.description: Silence before the sound, rounded to whole samples (as in kick-params).

peak_ceiling_dbfs.description: Peak ceiling of the quantised file.

preset.description: Name of the preset these values came from, if any.
